arxiv-2203-01314.title: Determination of coupling patterns by parallel searches for μ − → e + \mu^{-}\to e^{+} and μ − → e − \mu^{-}\to e^{-} in muonic atoms Preprint: STUPP-21-254, OCU-PHYS 559, NITEP 131
arxiv-2203-01314.creator: Joe Sato, Kohei Sugawara, Yuichi Uesaka, Masato Yamanaka
arxiv-2203-01314.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Joe Sato, Kohei Sugawara, Yuichi Uesaka, Masato Yamanaka. We investigate a possibility that the μ − → e + \mu^{-}\to e^{+} conversion is discovered prior to the μ − → e − \mu^{-}\to e^{-} conversion, and its implications to the new physics search. arxiv-2502-08085.description: Abstract Traditional methods for visualizing dynamic human expressions, particularly in medical training, often rely on flat-screen displays or static mannequins, which have proven inefficient for realistic simulation. Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems are increasingly deployed in safety-critical and networked environments, where they must operate reliably in the presence of malicious adversaries. While recent benchmarks have advanced the evaluation of large language model (LLM)-based UAV agents in terms of reasoning capability, navigation performance, and network efficiency, systematic assessment of security, resilience, and trust under adversarial conditions remains largely unexplored, particularly in emerging 6G-enabled settings.

pmc-13509755.creator: Deema Ibrahim Fallatah, Steve Christmas
pmc-13509755.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) establishes lifelong, asymptomatic persistence but frequently reactivates in renal transplant recipients, contributing to significant post-transplant morbidity. Although humoral responses are routinely monitored, the role of cellular immunity in viral control remains incompletely characterized. This study aimed to characterize BKPyV-specific T-cell responses and IgG-binding levels in healthy adults and renal transplant recipients and to explore their association with active BKPyV viruria.
